points.title: AI and ML Tooling
points.content: Kevin's AI and ML work is tied to practical interfaces and developer tools rather than isolated demos. The portfolio includes a Gemini-backed portfolio assistant, an expressive robot head using Whisper, llama.cpp, Zonos, Silero VAD, PyTorch, CUDA, ROS2, and OpenCV, plus AI coding-agent tools such as bento-ya, choomfie, clanker-spanker, and component-cop. His current role at Hamming AI is Software Engineer at a YC S24 startup building AI-powered developer tools.

points.title: How this chat assistant works
points.content:
This chat is a custom-built retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system, not a generic chatbot. It lives in src/lib/chat-knowledge.ts and a Next.js API route at /api/chat.

Pipeline per message:
1. Browser POSTs the conversation history to /api/chat (Vercel serverless function).
2. Upstash Redis rate-limits per visitor IP — sliding window of 10 sends per 60s. Returns HTTP 429 with a friendly fallback if exceeded.
3. Input is validated (message count cap of 20, per-message length cap of 4000 chars, total bytes cap of 50k).
4. A guardrail layer blocks off-topic queries and private-data probes using a regex blocklist plus an allow-list of public topics derived from portfolio.json.
5. For predictable openers (project rundowns, common suggested questions), the route returns a deterministic canned response — no LLM call, no quota burn.
6. For genuine follow-ups, a small in-memory keyword retriever scores each knowledge section against the query: +4 per keyword match, +1 per body-text match. Top 7 sections become the LLM's grounded context.
7. The route calls Google's Gemini API, walking a fallback chain (gemini-2.5-flash → gemini-2.0-flash → gemini-2.5-flash-lite → gemini-1.5-flash). Each model has its own free-tier daily quota, so chaining four stacks the effective ceiling to roughly 4250 requests per day at no cost.
8. The system prompt instructs the model to use only the provided context and refuse to invent details.

Stack:
- Frontend: React 19 + Tailwind in a custom 'terminal' panel inside the bentOS dashboard.
- API: Next.js 16 App Router route handler on Vercel serverless functions.
- LLM: Google Gemini Flash family via plain REST (no SDK, to keep the worker bundle small).
- Rate limiting: @upstash/ratelimit on top of Upstash Redis (free tier).
- Retrieval: deterministic keyword scoring over portfolio.json + projects/*.json + talking-points/*.json. No embeddings, no vector DB — overkill for ~50 sections and would cost money.

Why keyword retrieval instead of embeddings? Speed, determinism, zero cost, and the corpus is tiny and well-categorized. Embeddings would be the right call if there were thousands of documents or fuzzy semantic matching mattered, but for a portfolio chatbot the structured fields (project names, technologies, talking-point keywords) make exact-token matching very effective.

Why a fallback chain instead of one model? Each Gemini free-tier model has its own daily quota; chaining four means a single visitor would have to send thousands of messages before the chat fully degrades to demo mode. Auth errors fail fast (the same key wouldn't work on a different model); rate limit and server errors retry against the next model in the chain.

points.title: Education and Location
points.content: Kevin is based in Waterloo, Ontario, Canada and studies Computer Engineering at the University of Waterloo. His portfolio also includes work and project locations across Waterloo, Toronto, Austin, and Tokyo through education, internships, hackathons, and robotics research. The scrollable portfolio view visualizes these life and work locations on a globe.

points.title: Hackathon Projects
points.content: Kevin has several hackathon projects in the portfolio. ShoulderCupid won MLH Best Use of Solana at MakeUofT 2026. SnapFire won the Wolfram Alpha Award and Staff Picks at AliceHacks in November 2023. Kenesis, the AR gesture-controlled robot, was built at Hack the North 2025. These projects usually combine fast hardware prototyping with software, computer vision, or AI features under short timelines.

points.title: Hardware Prototyping
points.content: Kevin's hardware experience includes STM32 and ESP32 microcontrollers, PCB design in Altium, Arduino-based firmware, 3D printing, CAD in Fusion 360 and OnShape, soldering and assembly, servo and motor control, and sensor integration. His Midnight Sun experience focused on double-layer PCB routing, ERC/DRC-clean board work, and SMD soldering/testing. Several portfolio projects combine custom mechanical design with embedded electronics and real-time control.

points.title: Robotics Approach
points.content: Kevin's robotics work spans mechanical design, electronics, embedded control, ROS2, computer vision, and AI systems. His portfolio includes gesture-controlled robots, expressive robot heads, robotic arm puppeteering tools, haptic interfaces, and sensor-driven prototypes. A recurring pattern is building the full path from physical hardware to software control: CAD and 3D printing, PCB or microcontroller bring-up, perception with OpenCV or AprilTags, and higher-level control or AI behavior.

points.title: Portfolio Content Workflow
points.content: bentOS stores portfolio content as file-based JSON. Projects live in src/content/projects, talking points live in src/content/talking-points, and photography uses image files plus sidecar JSON under public/photos. The generated bundles are rebuilt by npm run sync. Choomfie-friendly scripts now provide deterministic commands for adding photos, projects, and chat talking points without hand-editing generated files.
